PROTOCOL 1: Provide psychoeducation to the person and their carers
Reduce stress and strengthen social supports
Promote functioning in daily activities and community life

If available, consider referring the person for brief psychological treatments such as interpersonal therapy (IPT), cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), behaviour activation, or problem-solving counselling
DO NOT manage the symptoms with ineffective treatments such as vitamin injections
BIPOLAR PROTOCOL: If a specialist is not immediately available, follow the treatment for depression (Protocol 1)
NEVER prescribe antidepressants alone without a mood stabilizer (such as lithium, carbamazepine, or valproate) because antidepressants can lead to mania in people with bipolar disorder
If symptoms of mania develop, tell the person and their carers to stop the antidepressant immediately and return for help
